# MM-P3-L3-HP03 - Maintenance manual - Machining hydraulic forging press #3

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Scope
This manual provides maintenance instructions for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03). It covers preventive maintenance tasks, inspection checkpoints, and corrective actions required to keep the press in safe, repeatable operating condition for machining operations. The procedures align with applicable safety practices and reference operational and service bulletins listed in Related Documents. The intent is to ensure mechanical integrity of the ram and hydraulic system and to document condition and repairs for traceability.

Tools
Required tools and consumables include industry-standard wrenches and sockets sized for the main ram bolt, a calibrated hydraulic pressure gauge compatible with the machine service port, inspection mirrors, LED inspection lights, clean lint-free rags, hydraulic system filter elements as specified by OEM guidance, approved hydraulic fluid as specified in the machine log, thread lubricant or anti-seize per OEM guidance, torque measurement device calibrated to traceable standards, and personal protective equipment consistent with plant policy. Use the torque measurement device to verify the main ram bolt torque stated below.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
Shut down the press per plant lockout/tagout requirements and relieve hydraulic pressure through the machine service ports. Verify energy isolation and post appropriate signs. Consult SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03 for operator-level shutdown and startup sequences and for specific machine safety interlocks before beginning maintenance.

Visual inspection
Inspect the ram, gland, seals, and surrounds for evidence of leakage, scoring, or abnormal wear. Use inspection mirrors and LED lights to examine the ram surface beyond the visible area. Record any fluid or metal contamination found on rags after wiping the ram. Check fasteners for corrosion and movement by hand prior to torque verification.

Hydraulic system pressure verification
Connect a calibrated hydraulic pressure gauge to the approved service port and slowly prime the gauge per manufacturer instructions. Confirm the system pressure does not exceed the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) which is 295 bar. If system pressure is at or above the system pressure limit, stop and consult hydraulic service procedures and Related Documents before further operation.

Main ram bolt verification and torque
Access the main ram retention bolt per machine disassembly guidance. Clean bolt threads and seating surfaces of debris and contamination. Using a calibrated torque measurement device, verify the main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. If the measured torque is below specification, apply thread lubricant or anti-seize as required by OEM guidance and torque the bolt to the specified value using a calibrated torque tool. If the bolt cannot reach or maintain the specified torque, record the condition, secure the machine, and escalate to mechanical engineering for further evaluation.

Seal and gland service
If seals or gland components are worn or leaking, follow OEM replacement steps, taking care to maintain cleanliness to prevent contamination of the hydraulic system. Use lint-free materials for wiping and ensure replacement parts conform to machine specifications. After reassembly, perform a pressure verification and leak test as described above.

Functional verification
After mechanical tasks are complete and energy is restored per SOP-P3-L3-02 and SOP-P3-L3-03, run a controlled test cycle per operational guidance using the documented startup procedure. Monitor for abnormal noises, seal leakage, or drifting pressures. Confirm repeatability of ram movement and that no external fluid appears at gland or bolt interfaces.

Records and documentation
Maintain a maintenance entry in the machine history log describing work performed, observations, parts replaced, measurements taken, and the names of personnel performing the work. Attach calibrated torque device and pressure gauge calibration certificates to the maintenance record when used for verification. Use the Related Documents section to link work to applicable SOPs and service bulletins.

Acceptance criteria
The press is acceptable to return to service when the following conditions are met:
- No external hydraulic leakage is present at the ram gland, bolt interfaces, or hydraulic connections after reassembly and test cycle.
- The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m as verified with a calibrated tool.
- System pressure during functional verification does not exceed the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) which is 295 bar.
- Operational performance of the ram is consistent with pre-maintenance behavior and no abnormal noises or vibrations are observed during controlled test cycles.
- All maintenance actions and measurements are recorded in the equipment history log and calibration certificates are filed with the maintenance record.

Background and rationale
Maintaining correct clamping and torque on the main ram bolt is critical to ensure axial preload and to prevent relative movement that can cause accelerated wear of the ram surface and seal damage. Verifying that hydraulic pressure remains below the system pressure limit protects system components and safety devices from overpressure conditions. Measuring and recording these parameters provide a defensible maintenance history that supports root cause analysis if repeat failures occur.

Examples and real-world notes
Example entries in the maintenance log should include the exact measured torque value as read from the calibrated instrument and the make/model of the torque device, along with the calibrated pressure gauge reading observed during verification. If a pressure spike occurred during test cycling, note the conditions that produced the spike and reference SB-1011 for any bulletin-specific guidance. When repeated torque loss or pressure excursions are observed, escalate per plant mechanical engineering policy.

Records to keep
Retain the maintenance work order, the equipment history log entry, calibration certificates for torque and pressure instruments, parts replaced invoices, and any photos documenting condition. File all records in the document control system under this manual’s document id for traceability.

Related documents
SB-1011  
SOP-P3-L3-02  
SOP-P3-L3-03
